title: Helm preflight validator and on-prem hotpatch to remediate operator upgrade drift
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Several Private/VPC customers reported failed operator upgrades during a recent maintenance window. Symptoms: post-upgrade controller pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff, CRDs present but mismatched schema versions, and Helm post-upgrade hooks timing out which left resources partially migrated and caused application traffic outages for affected tenants. Root cause analysis found a combination of (1) a Helm chart change that introduced a preupgrade validation hook which assumed a CRD field that does not exist in older clusters, and (2) a controller start-up path that treated missing optional fields as fatal instead of graceful fallbacks, which produced state drift between Helm release values and live cluster resource fields.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Automated preflight validation runs during chart upgrade and catches schema skews with clear remediation guidance; 2) Hotfix operator image (3.6.1-hotfix) starts gracefully when optional fields are absent and records a non-fatal compatibility warning; 3) All escalated customer clusters upgraded successfully to operator-3.6.1-hotfix with no degraded pods post-upgrade; 4) Runbook updated with rollback and remediation commands and shared with SEs and support; 5) Postmortem and follow-ups created and assigned.
steps_to_reproduce: Bootstrap clean on-prem cluster running operator-3.4.2 with legacy CRD schema
Install operator-3.4.2 and create sample InferenceCluster CRs following older schema fields
Attempt helm upgrade to operator-3.6.0 which includes the new preupgrade validation hook
Observe helm upgrade hang during hook, controller pods crash due to strict validation, and partial CRD migration leaving live objects with missing fields
Run kubectl describe on failing pods and check helm release status to see hook timeout and partial release state
mitigation_steps: Immediate: Instruct affected customers to suspend Helm post-upgrade hooks and restart the operator with environment flag OPERATOR_COMPAT_WARNING=1 to allow graceful startup
Hotpatch: Build operator-3.6.1-hotfix that relaxes strict validation for optional fields and short-circuits the preupgrade hook fallback path
Helm: Publish patched chart operator-chart-3.6.1-hotfix that includes a preflight --dry-run flag and more defensive hook logic
Rollback: Document helm rollback command sequence and safe-state checkpoint commands (kubectl patch CRD to restore expected fields) in runbook
Customer communications: Notify impacted customers with step-by-step remediate doc and offer hands-on upgrade assistance and credit for incident

postmortem_actions: Add automated preflight validation to the chart publishing pipeline and gate major upgrades (owner: infra)
Ship a config-drift detector service that periodically validates live cluster CRs against pinned schemas and surfaces drift alerts in Console (owner: serving-runtime)
Add e2e test for helm upgrade path covering old CRD versions and include in CI matrix
Update runbooks and create a support playbook with canned customer remediation steps and escalation contacts
Audit Helm hooks across charts for side effects and make them idempotent (owner: charts-team)
notes: This incident was distinct from previous operator helm failures because it combined a new preupgrade hook with strict runtime validation; previous incidents were often purely helm sequencing or leader-election related.
We intentionally kept the hotfix small: non-breaking leniency on optional fields and safer hook timeouts. A follow-up will formalize schema migration tooling rather than permissive start-up behavior.
Support provided live upgrade assistance for two enterprise customers who had heavy custom CRs; both required a short manual patch to rehydrate legacy fields before the final upgrade step.
Legal and compliance teams reviewed the customer notification language prior to sending due to several affected enterprise accounts
